complexity.notes: Correct but quadratic: the inner loop rewrites the whole remaining range on every one of the ~n pointer moves. The classic O(n) version only updates the single position being passed (tracking running left/right maxima), which would drop the inner loop entirely. Logic is sound — when the lower side's running bottleneck v is established, the opposite pointer necessarily rests at a bar of height >= v while the range still covers i, so water[i] reaches min(maxLeft[i], maxRight[i]).
complexity.summary: A two-pointer narrowing scheme: each step floods the entire current range [start, end] with min(height[start], height[end]) into a water array (taking max), then advances whichever boundary bar is lower. Effectively this computes min(maxLeft[i], maxRight[i]) - height[i] for every bar, but pays O(n) per pointer move.
